# Strapi Plugin IO — Full Documentation (llms-full.txt)

========== https://strapi-community.github.io/plugin-io/ ==========

## Quick start

```bash
npm install @strapi-community/plugin-io
```

```js
// config/plugins.js
module.exports = {
  io: { enabled: true, config: { contentTypes: ['api::article.article'] } },
};
```

Give the Public role **find** on Article, then:

```js
import { io } from 'socket.io-client';

const socket = io('http://localhost:1337');
socket.on('article:publish', ({ data }) => console.log('Published:', data.attributes.title));
```

[Full getting started guide →](/guide/getting-started)

## Built like a native Strapi screen

Settings and Monitoring live under _Settings > Socket.IO_ and follow the
layout of Strapi's own settings pages: Save in the header, an unsaved-changes
guard, inline validation, confirmation dialogs and RBAC-aware actions, in
light and dark mode and five languages.

![Settings > Socket.IO > Settings](/settings.png)

![Monitoring in dark mode](/monitoring-dark.png)

![Monitoring at 390 px width](/monitoring-mobile.png)

The homepage gets two widgets through Strapi's Widget API, and the Content
Manager edit view shows who else is editing.

![Socket.IO homepage widget](/widget.png)

![Live presence panel in the edit view](/presence.png)

Screenshots come from a local test host with synthetic data.

## Who receives what

| Client                  | Joins                 | Receives                                                                  |
| ----------------------- | --------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| No token                | `io-role-public`      | Types the Public role may `find` (unless authentication is required)      |
| Users & Permissions JWT | `io-role-` | Types the user's role may `find`                                          |
| Content API token       | `io-token-`       | Read-only and full-access: all watched types; custom: types it may `find` |
| Admin (presence panel)  | `io-admin-`       | Presence only, never content events                                       |

## Security and performance

- Admin routes need an authenticated admin plus the plugin permission. Monitoring responses contain counts and display names only.
- Content events are sanitized per audience; rooms without listeners are skipped before sanitizing.
- Socket re-checks run in one batch per kind (one query for all users, tokens or admins), triggered right away when a user, token, admin or Strapi session changes.
- Strapi's Data Transfer WebSocket (`strapi transfer`) keeps working next to Socket.IO (#112).

## Requirements

- Strapi 5.13 or later (tested with 5.61)
- Node.js 22 or 24
- Socket.IO 4.8 clients (`socket.io-client`)

## Community

- [Report an issue](https://github.com/strapi-community/plugin-io/issues)
- [Source on GitHub](https://github.com/strapi-community/plugin-io)
- [Related plugins](/ecosystem)

========== https://strapi-community.github.io/plugin-io/guide/getting-started ==========

# Getting started

From `npm install` to your first live event in about a minute.

## Requirements

|                     | Version                                                  |
| ------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------- |
| Strapi              | 5.13 or later (tested with 5.61)                         |
| Node.js             | 22.21+ or 24.9+ (up to 26, like Strapi 5.61)             |
| Users & Permissions | Optional. Needed for user JWTs and the Public role room. |

For Strapi 4 use version 2.x of the plugin.

## 1. Install

```bash [npm]
npm install @strapi-community/plugin-io
```

```bash [yarn]
yarn add @strapi-community/plugin-io
```

```bash [pnpm]
pnpm add @strapi-community/plugin-io
```

## 2. Watch a content type

```js [config/plugins.js]
module.exports = () => ({
  io: {
    enabled: true,
    config: {
      contentTypes: ['api::article.article'],
    },
  },
});
```

```ts [config/plugins.ts]
export default () => ({
  io: {
    enabled: true,
    config: {
      contentTypes: ['api::article.article'],
    },
  },
});
```

Restart Strapi (`npm run develop`).

## 3. Allow reading

Clients receive what they may read through the REST API. For a quick test,
give the **Public** role the **find** permission for Article in
_Settings > Users & Permissions plugin > Roles > Public_.

## 4. Listen

```bash
npm install socket.io-client
```

```js
import { io } from 'socket.io-client';

const socket = io('http://localhost:1337');

socket.on('connect', () => console.log('connected', socket.id));
socket.on('article:publish', ({ data }) => console.log('published', data.attributes.title));
socket.on('article:delete', ({ data }) => console.log('deleted', data.documentId));
```

Publish an article in the Content Manager and watch the event arrive.

A page served from another origin (for example `http://localhost:3000`) must be
listed under _Settings > Socket.IO > Settings > Allowed origins_. Node scripts
and mobile apps send no `Origin` header and are not affected.

## Authenticate clients

```js
// Users & Permissions JWT: the client joins its role's room
const socket = io(url, { auth: (cb) => cb({ strategy: 'jwt', token: getJwt() }) });

// Content API token (read-only, full-access or custom)
const socket = io(url, { auth: { strategy: 'api-token', token: process.env.STRAPI_TOKEN } });
```

A function for `auth` runs on every reconnect, so a refreshed JWT is picked up.
Turn on _Require authentication_ to refuse clients without a token. Failed
handshakes only ever see `Authentication failed`.

## What you get in the admin

- **Settings > Socket.IO > Settings**: origins, limits, security, content events, roles, presence and monitoring. Changes apply without a restart.
- **Settings > Socket.IO > Monitoring**: connected clients, rooms, events per second, admins online and the recent event log.
- **Homepage widgets**: _Socket.IO_ counters and _Admins online_ (Strapi 5.13+).
- **Live presence** in the Content Manager edit view.

Super Admins see everything. Grant the plugin's permissions to other roles in
_Settings > Administration panel > Roles > Plugins > IO_.

![Settings > Socket.IO > Settings](/settings.png)

## Troubleshooting

**Nothing arrives.** Check that the role or token has `find` on the content
type, that the content type is watched, and, with Draft & Publish, that you
listen to `:publish` (drafts are not sent while _Only published content_ is on).

**`connect_error: Authentication failed`.** The JWT or token is invalid,
expired or belongs to a blocked user. After 20 failures from one IP within a
minute, that IP is locked out for the rest of the minute.

**Browser shows a CORS error or a 400/403 on `/socket.io/`.** Add the page's
origin under _Allowed origins_.

**`strapi transfer` stopped working.** Upgrade to 6.0; see the
[README troubleshooting](https://github.com/strapi-community/plugin-io#troubleshooting) for #112.

## Next steps

- [Content types](/examples/content-types): actions, populate, payloads
- [Custom events](/examples/events): handle client events safely
- [Plugin configuration](/api/plugin-config): every option
- [Migration guide](/guide/migration): upgrading from 5.x


========== https://strapi-community.github.io/plugin-io/guide/widget ==========

# Homepage widgets

The plugin adds two widgets to the Strapi admin homepage through the official Widget API (Strapi 5.13 and later). They look and behave like Strapi's own widgets and can be arranged or removed with **Add Widget** on the homepage.

Both widgets need the admin permission **Read monitoring** (`plugin::io.monitoring.read`). Super Admins have it; grant it to other roles under _Settings > Administration panel > Roles > Plugins > IO > Monitoring_.

---

## Socket.IO

![Socket.IO homepage widget](/widget.png)

Laid out like the native _Project statistics_ widget: four cells, each opening _Settings > Socket.IO > Monitoring_.

| Cell              | Meaning                                                                     |
| ----------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Connected clients | Sockets connected right now (admins, users, API tokens and public clients). |
| Admins online     | Admins with the Content Manager open.                                       |
| Events per second | Average over the last 10 seconds.                                           |
| Events sent       | Events emitted since the last restart or reset.                             |

The widget refreshes every 15 seconds.

## Admins online

![Admins online homepage widget](/admins-online-widget.png)

Laid out like the native _Last edited entries_ widget: one row per other admin with the Content Manager open, the content type they are editing and when they connected. Click a row or the edit button to open the same entry. Your own session is not listed. The widget refreshes every 15 seconds.

The list contains names only. Emails, IP addresses and socket ids are never sent to the browser. Entries in content types you may not read in the Content Manager are not named: the row says _An entry you cannot view_ instead (Monitoring shows a count).

---

## States

- **Loading** and **error** use Strapi's native widget states. On an error, **Try again** reloads the data.
- **Admins online** shows "No other admins are editing right now." when nobody else is editing.
- When the presence feature is off in the settings, nobody appears in _Admins online_.

## Monitoring page

![Settings > Socket.IO > Monitoring](/monitoringSettings.png)

_Settings > Socket.IO > Monitoring_ shows the same counters with a breakdown by client type, the admins online with the entries they edit, and the event log (turn on **Keep an event log** in the settings). Roles with **Reset statistics and send test events** (`plugin::io.monitoring.manage`) can send a test event and reset the statistics.

## Troubleshooting

**The widgets do not appear.** Check that your Strapi version is 5.13 or later and that your role has `plugin::io.monitoring.read`. Then rebuild the admin (`npm run build`).

**Connected clients stays at 0.** No client is connected. Connect one and wait for the next refresh:

```javascript
import { io } from 'socket.io-client';

const socket = io('http://localhost:1337', { transports: ['websocket'] });
socket.on('connect', () => console.log('connected', socket.id));
```

**Admins online is empty while someone edits.** **Show who is editing** must be on (_Settings > Socket.IO > Settings > Live presence_), and the other admin needs read permission for that content type in the Content Manager.

## See also

- [Getting Started](/guide/getting-started)
- [IO class](/api/io-class)
- [Configuration](/api/plugin-config)


========== https://strapi-community.github.io/plugin-io/guide/migration ==========

# Migration guide

## Compatibility

| Plugin | Strapi        | Node.js                   | Status   |
| ------ | ------------- | ------------------------- | -------- |
| 6.x    | 5.13 or later | 22.21+ or 24.9+ (to 26.x) | Current  |
| 5.x    | 5.x           | 18 to 22                  | Previous |
| 2.x    | 4.x           | 14 to 20                  | Legacy   |

6.x needs Node.js 22.21 or 24.9 (or newer): the plugin uses the HTTP
server's `shouldUpgradeCallback`, added in those releases, to leave every
non-Socket.IO request, including upgrade requests with a body, to Strapi
exactly as Node would without the plugin.

## 5.x to 6.0

6.0 makes delivery follow Strapi's read permissions and enforces the admin
settings. Work through the list below after upgrading.

### 1. Read permission decides delivery

Roles and API tokens receive events for content types they may `find` or
`findOne`. Create or update permissions alone no longer deliver anything.

**Do:** in _Settings > Users & Permissions > Roles_ (and for custom API
tokens), grant `find` on every content type a client should receive.

### 2. Publish has its own events

Publishing used to emit `:delete` followed by `:create`. It now emits
`:publish`. Unpublish and discard draft emit `:unpublish` and `:discardDraft`.

```js
// before
socket.on('article:create', add);
socket.on('article:delete', remove);

// after
socket.on('article:publish', add);
socket.on('article:unpublish', ({ data }) => remove(data.documentId));
socket.on('article:delete', ({ data }) => remove(data.documentId));
```

If `config.contentTypes[].actions` lists actions, add the new ones you need.

### 3. Drafts are not sent by default

With Draft & Publish, only published versions are sent. Turn off
_Only published content_ in the settings to also send drafts to the roles
that may read them.

### 4. Delete events go to readers only

`:delete` and `:unpublish` are sent only to roles and tokens that may read the
content type, as `{ data: { documentId, locale? } }`, one event per locale.

### 5. Room names

| Room                   | 5.x                                       | 6.0                   |
| ---------------------- | ----------------------------------------- | --------------------- |
| Public / Authenticated | `io-role-public`, `io-role-authenticated` | unchanged             |
| Custom role            | `io-role-`       | `io-role-` |
| API token              | `io-token-`     | `io-token-` |

Names are now stable when a role or token is renamed, and two tokens with the
same name no longer share a room.

### 6. `socket.data` for your handlers

The handshake fills `socket.data`. Check `socket.data.kind` before you use an id:

| `kind`   | Keys                                            |
| -------- | ----------------------------------------------- |
| `user`   | `user.id`, `user.role`, `role`, `expiresAt`     |
| `token`  | `token.id`, `token.type`, `expiresAt`           |
| `public` | `role`                                          |
| `admin`  | `admin.id`, `admin.firstname`, `admin.lastname` |

Admin presence sockets (from the Content Manager) keep their identity under
`socket.data.admin`, never under `socket.data.user`, and your `config.events`
handlers do not run on them unless the event sets `admin: true`. Keys that
older docs mentioned, such as `socket.data.userId` or
`socket.data.user.username`, were never set by the plugin.

### 7. `hooks.init`

- The context is `{ strapi, $io, io }`; `$io` and `io` are the same object, so both old and new examples work.
- `init` runs **before** the plugin handshake is added, as in 5.x. Middleware from `$io.server.use()` therefore runs before authentication, and `socket.data.kind` is not set yet inside it. Use a `connection` handler in `config.events` for logic that needs the authenticated client.
- Do not overwrite `socket.data.user` or `socket.data.kind` in middleware; the handshake sets them afterwards.

### 8. Allowed origins are enforced for WebSocket too

With an empty _Allowed origins_ list, browsers may only connect from the
Strapi host itself or from the origins of `server.url` / `admin.url`. 5.x
accepted WebSocket connections from any origin. Clients without an `Origin`
header (Node, mobile apps) are not affected.

**Do:** add every frontend origin, for example `https://app.example.com`,
under _Settings > Socket.IO > Allowed origins_.

### 9. Sockets end with their session

- User sockets are disconnected when the JWT expires, the user is blocked or changes role, and (refresh mode) when the Strapi session behind the access token is revoked or the user logs out.
- API-token sockets end when the token is deleted or expires.
- Admin presence sockets end when the admin logs out, the admin session expires, the account is deactivated, or the admin loses read access to an entry the panel has open.

### 10. Settings and permissions

- Stored 5.x settings are migrated on the first start and are now enforced. Keys that were never implemented (Redis, namespaces, live preview, field-level changes) are dropped. The 5.x entity subscription limit is kept, but entity subscriptions stay off until you turn them on. The old default origin `http://localhost:3000` and the old default limit of 1000 connections are reset.
- Only Super Admins see the plugin pages until you grant `Read settings`, `Update settings`, `Read monitoring` and `Reset statistics and send test events` under _Settings > Administration panel > Roles > Plugins > IO_.

### 11. Restored, changed and removed

**Entity subscriptions** are back, now with Strapi permissions:

- Turn them on under _Settings > Socket.IO > Entry subscriptions_. They are off by default.
- Clients send `subscribe-entity` with `{ uid, documentId }`. `{ uid, id }` still works, but `id` must be the `documentId`; numeric ids are refused.
- A subscription needs `find` or `findOne` for the content type on the client's own role or API token, and the entry must exist (published, while _Only published content_ is on).
- Subscribers receive events of content types and actions that are not broadcast under _Events_. Each event is sanitized with the subscriber's role or token permissions, and read permission is checked again on every event.
- Server helpers: `strapi.$io.subscribeToEntity()`, `unsubscribeFromEntity()`, `getEntitySubscriptions()`. `emitToEntity` and `getEntityRoomSockets` are not part of 6.0.

**Settings export and import** are back on the settings page. The file is the
settings JSON (no secrets). Import checks it on the server, shows the changed
values, fills the form, and nothing is stored until _Save_.

| Removed                      | Replacement and reason                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| ---------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `security` service           | The settings _Allowed/blocked IPs_, _Limit client events_, _Maximum connections_                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| Redis toggle in the settings | Attach `@socket.io/redis-adapter` in `hooks.init`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| Live preview events          | Not restored. 5.x relayed unsaved field values from the editor to clients. Unsaved values never pass through the Document Service, so Strapi's Content API sanitizer cannot check them per role or token, and a private field would reach clients that may not read it. Use Strapi's [Preview](https://docs.strapi.io/cms/features/preview), or turn off _Only published content_ and subscribe to the entry to receive saved drafts. |
| Field-level diffs            | Not restored. A diff needs the previous version of every updated entry (one extra query per update) and has to be computed on each audience's sanitized data, or changed field names would reveal private fields. Compare the entry you receive with the one you have on the client.                                                                                                                                                  |
| `GET /api/io`                | None (it answered 500)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |

### 12. Smaller changes

- Node.js 22.0 to 22.20 and 23 are no longer supported. The 400 answer that older Node.js versions gave upgrade requests with a body is gone with them.
- `maxHttpBufferSize` defaults to 100 KB. Raise it in `socket.serverOptions` if clients send larger messages.
- The `POST /io/presence/session` admin route keeps at most five unused tokens per admin and answers `429` when 10,000 are pending server-wide.
- _Monitoring > Admins online_ and the _Admins online_ widget list only entries in content types the viewer may read; the rest are counted as "entries you cannot view".

## v2 (Strapi 4) to v5 (Strapi 5)

1. Upgrade Strapi itself first with the [official upgrade tool](https://docs.strapi.io/cms/upgrade-tool):
   `npx @strapi/upgrade major`.
2. Install the plugin version for Strapi 5: `npm install @strapi-community/plugin-io@latest`.
3. Keep `config/plugins.js`; the `contentTypes`, `events`, `hooks` and `socket` keys have the same shape.
4. Replace `strapi.entityService` calls in your event handlers with the [Document Service](https://docs.strapi.io/cms/api/document-service) (`strapi.documents(uid)`), which identifies entries by `documentId`.
5. Then follow the 5.x to 6.0 steps above.

## Getting help

Search or open an issue on [GitHub](https://github.com/strapi-community/plugin-io/issues).
Include your Strapi version, plugin version, Node.js version and the
smallest config that reproduces the problem.

## Dependency advisories (development tree)

`npm audit --omit=dev` is clean: the published package does not contain any
of the packages below. The repository's development tree overrides
`nodemailer` (^10.3.1), `zod` under `koa-body` (^4.6.7) and
`@hono/node-server` under `@modelcontextprotocol/node` (^2.1.6). These
remain, because no compatible patched release exists:

| Package (path)                                                                   | Advisory                                                      | Why it stays                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| -------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `zod` 3.25 in `koa-session` 7 (`@strapi/core`)                                   | GHSA-mrhx-c7xc-m3w5 (high)                                    | Fixed in zod 4.6.6, but koa-session uses `z.function().args()`, which zod 4 removed. Needs a Strapi release.                                                                                      |
| `stream-json` 1.9 (`@strapi/data-transfer`)                                      | GHSA-528h-pc64-c93x, GHSA-hqr4-qq8f-hg3x, GHSA-mjw6-4jj6-33hc | Fixed in 3.6; 3.x is a new major with a changed API. Needs a Strapi release.                                                                                                                      |
| `react-router` 6 (peer of the Strapi 5 admin)                                    | GHSA-wrjc-x8rr-h8h6, GHSA-337j-9hxr-rhxg                      | Fixed in 7.18; the Strapi 5 admin runs on react-router-dom 6.                                                                                                                                     |
| `minimatch` 9/10 and `glob` 13 (ESLint, nodemon, api-extractor, Strapi CLI, npm) | GHSA-g3hv-75wg-m249, GHSA-3g3m-2fjr-6pw4                      | Fixed in minimatch 11 / glob 14, which remove APIs (`makeRe`, `Minimatch#regexp`) that typedoc still calls; npm's bundled copies cannot be overridden. Build tooling only, with trusted patterns. |
| `deepmerge` 4.3.1                                                                | GHSA-gcqx-w48m-w2h4 (low)                                     | No patched release.                                                                                                                                                                               |

The other entries `npm audit` lists (`@strapi/*`, `eslint`, `semantic-release`,
`@semantic-release/*`, `@strapi/sdk-plugin`) are flagged only because they
depend on the packages above.


========== https://strapi-community.github.io/plugin-io/api/io-class ==========

# IO class (`strapi.$io`)

The plugin creates one `SocketIO` instance during bootstrap and exposes it as
`strapi.$io`. Use it from services, controllers, lifecycles or cron jobs.

## Quick reference

```js
await strapi.$io.emit({ event, schema, data }); // content event, sanitized per audience
await strapi.$io.emitIdentifier({ event, schema, data: { documentId, locale } });
await strapi.$io.raw({ event, data, rooms }); // custom event, sensitive keys removed

strapi.$io.joinRoom(socketId, room); // false for plugin rooms
strapi.$io.leaveRoom(socketId, room);
await strapi.$io.getSocketsInRoom(room); // socket ids
strapi.$io.sendPrivateMessage(socketId, event, data);
strapi.$io.broadcast(socketId, event, data); // everyone except socketId
strapi.$io.emitToNamespace('chat', event, data);
strapi.$io.disconnectSocket(socketId);
await strapi.$io.revalidateSockets(kinds?, { ids? });
await strapi.$io.subscribeToEntity(socketId, uid, documentId); // same checks as subscribe-entity
strapi.$io.unsubscribeFromEntity(socketId, uid, documentId);
strapi.$io.getEntitySubscriptions(socketId);

strapi.$io.server; // Socket.IO Server
strapi.$io.namespaces; // { '': Namespace, chat: Namespace }
```

## `emit()`

Sends a content event to every role and API token that may read the content
type (`find` or `findOne`). Each audience receives the entry sanitized with its
own permissions. If sanitizing fails for an audience, that audience is skipped.

```ts
emit(options: { event: string; schema: string | { uid: string; singularName?: string }; data: object }): Promise
```

- The event name is `:`, for example `article:update`.
- Returns the number of rooms that received the event. With the default in-memory adapter, rooms without sockets are skipped before sanitizing and not counted.
- The payload is `{ data: { id, attributes }, meta: {} }`.

```js
const entry = await strapi.documents('api::article.article').findOne({ documentId, populate: ['author'] });
await strapi.$io.emit({ event: 'update', schema: 'api::article.article', data: entry });
```

The plugin calls `emit()` itself for watched content types, so you only need
it for content you do not watch or events you build yourself.

## `emitIdentifier()`

Sends `{ data: { documentId, locale? } }` to the audiences that may read the
type. The plugin uses it for `delete` and `unpublish`.

```js
await strapi.$io.emitIdentifier({
  event: 'delete',
  schema: 'api::article.article',
  data: { documentId, locale: 'en' },
});
```

## `raw()`

Sends a custom event as `{ data }`. Keys from the sensitive field list are
removed first. Without `rooms` the event goes to every connected client of the
default namespace.

```ts
raw(options: { event: string; data: unknown; rooms?: string[] }): Promise
```

```js
await strapi.$io.raw({ event: 'maintenance', data: { startsAt: '22:00 UTC' } });
await strapi.$io.raw({ event: 'report:ready', data: { id }, rooms: [`user-${userId}`] });
```

`raw()` does not check permissions. Choose the rooms yourself.

## Room helpers

| Method                                      | Returns             | Notes                                                                   |
| ------------------------------------------- | ------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `joinRoom(socketId, room)`                  | `boolean`           | `false` when the socket is unknown or the room belongs to the plugin.   |
| `leaveRoom(socketId, room)`                 | `boolean`           | `false` when the socket is unknown.                                     |
| `getSocketsInRoom(room)`                    | `Promise` | Socket ids, across instances when an adapter such as Redis is attached. |
| `sendPrivateMessage(socketId, event, data)` | `void`              | Sends `data` as is (no sanitizing).                                     |
| `broadcast(socketId, event, data)`          | `void`              | Everyone except `socketId`.                                             |
| `emitToNamespace(namespace, event, data)`   | `void`              | `namespace` with or without the leading slash.                          |
| `disconnectSocket(socketId)`                | `boolean`           | Closes the connection.                                                  |

Plugin rooms (`io-role-`, `io-token-`, `io-admin-`, `io-entity-`, `presence:`) cannot be
joined with `joinRoom()`.

## `revalidateSockets()`

Re-checks authenticated sockets and disconnects those whose credentials are no
longer valid: expired or invalid JWT, blocked user, changed role, revoked
Strapi session, deleted or expired API token, deactivated admin, or an admin
who lost read access to an entry the presence panel has open.

```ts
revalidateSockets(kinds?: Array, options?: { ids?: Iterable }): Promise
```

```js
await strapi.$io.revalidateSockets(); // everything
await strapi.$io.revalidateSockets(['user'], { ids: [userId] }); // one user's sockets
```

Returns the number of disconnected sockets. Sockets are checked in one batch
per kind (one query for all users, one for all tokens, one for all admins).
The plugin already runs this every five minutes and right after users, admins,
API tokens or Strapi sessions change, so you rarely need to call it.

## `server` and `namespaces`

```js
strapi.$io.server.emit('hello', { ok: true }); // the Socket.IO Server, no sanitizing
strapi.$io.server.to('io-role-authenticated').emit('notice', { text: 'Hi' });
Object.keys(strapi.$io.namespaces); // ['', 'chat']
```

Namespaces created with `strapi.$io.server.of('/name')` get the plugin
handshake. Content events go to the default namespace only.

## Monitoring service

Counts only, never IP addresses, emails, tokens or socket ids:

```js
const monitoring = strapi.plugin('io').service('monitoring');
await monitoring.getConnectionStats(); // { connected, rooms, byKind: { admin, user, token, public } }
monitoring.getEventStats(); // { totalEvents, eventsPerSecond, lastEventAt, totalConnections, since }
monitoring.getEventLog(50); // newest first, when the event log is on
```

## Client payloads

```js
socket.on('article:update', ({ data }) => render(data.attributes)); // emit()
socket.on('article:delete', ({ data }) => remove(data.documentId)); // emitIdentifier()
socket.on('maintenance', ({ data }) => banner(data.startsAt)); // raw()
```

## TypeScript

The package ships `types.d.ts` and adds `$io` to `Core.Strapi`:

```ts
import type { SocketIOConfig, SocketData } from '@strapi-community/plugin-io/strapi-server';

const config: SocketIOConfig = { contentTypes: ['api::article.article'] };

const handler = (_ctx: unknown, socket: { data: SocketData }) => {
  if (socket.data.kind === 'user') console.log(socket.data.user?.id);
};
```

## Entity subscriptions

Clients can follow single entries once _Settings > Socket.IO > Entry
subscriptions_ is on. Each subscription is checked against the read
permission of the client's own role or API token, and every event is
sanitized with those permissions. Subscribers also receive events of content
types and actions that are not broadcast under _Events_; a client that is in
both its role room and an entry room receives each event once.

```js
// client
socket.emit('subscribe-entity', { uid: 'api::article.article', documentId }, (reply) => {
  // { success: true, uid, documentId, id } or { success: false, error }
});
socket.on('article:update', ({ data }) => render(data.attributes));
socket.emit('unsubscribe-entity', { uid: 'api::article.article', documentId });
socket.emit('get-entity-subscriptions', ({ subscriptions }) => console.log(subscriptions));
```

| Error                                                 | Meaning                                                                        |
| ----------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `Entity subscriptions are disabled`                   | The setting is off.                                                            |
| `Invalid parameters: uid and documentId are required` | `uid` is not an `api::` uid or `documentId` is not a document id.              |
| `Not allowed`                                         | Admin socket, unknown content type, or no `find`/`findOne` for the role/token. |
| `Entity not found`                                    | No such entry (published only, while _Only published content_ is on).          |
| `Maximum subscriptions (n) reached`                   | The per-client limit from the settings.                                        |
| `Rate limit exceeded`                                 | More than ten subscribe requests per second.                                   |

Server code can use the same checks:

| Method                                             | Returns                                                           |
| -------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `subscribeToEntity(socketId, uid, documentId)`     | `Promise` |
| `unsubscribeFromEntity(socketId, uid, documentId)` | `{ success, uid, documentId, id } \| { success, error }`          |
| `getEntitySubscriptions(socketId)`                 | `{ success, subscriptions: [{ uid, documentId, id }] }`           |

`emit()` and `emitIdentifier()` accept `broadcast: false` to reach only the
subscribers of `data.documentId`.

## Not part of 6.0

`emitToEntity`, `getEntityRoomSockets`, live preview field events
(`preview:*`) and field-level diffs. See the
[migration guide](../guide/migration.md#_11-restored-changed-and-removed) for
the reasons.

## See also

- [Plugin configuration](/api/plugin-config)
- [Custom events](/examples/events)
- [Socket.IO server API](https://socket.io/docs/v4/server-api/)


========== https://strapi-community.github.io/plugin-io/api/plugin-config ==========

# Plugin configuration

The plugin reads `config/plugins.js` (or `.ts`) once at startup. Everything an
editor may change at runtime lives in the admin settings instead, see
[Admin settings](#admin-settings).

```js
// config/plugins.js
module.exports = ({ env }) => ({
  io: {
    enabled: true,
    config: {
      contentTypes: ['api::article.article'],
      sensitiveFields: [],
      events: [],
      hooks: {},
      socket: { serverOptions: {} },
    },
  },
});
```

The config is validated at startup. An unknown shape (for example a handler
that is not a function) stops Strapi with a validation error.

## Options

| Option                 | Type                                       | Default | Description                                                                                    |
| ---------------------- | ------------------------------------------ | ------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `contentTypes`         | `Array`       | `[]`    | Content types whose changes are sent. More can be added in the admin settings.                 |
| `sensitiveFields`      | `string[]`                                 | `[]`    | Extra field names that are never sent, on top of the built-in list.                            |
| `events`               | `Array`         | `[]`    | Handlers for events your clients send. See [Custom events](/examples/events).                  |
| `hooks.init`           | `({ strapi, $io, io }) => void \| Promise` | none    | Runs once during bootstrap, before the handshake. See [Hooks](/examples/hooks).                |
| `socket.serverOptions` | Socket.IO `ServerOptions`                  | `{}`    | Passed to `new Server()`. Values set here win over the plugin defaults and the admin settings. |

## `contentTypes`

A string watches every action. An object narrows the actions or adds
relations.

```js
contentTypes: [
  'api::article.article',
  { uid: 'api::page.page', actions: ['publish', 'unpublish', 'delete'] },
  { uid: 'api::product.product', populate: ['category', 'images'] },
],
```

| Key        | Type                                                                                    | Default  | Description                                                                                                                                                                     |
| ---------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `uid`      | `string`                                                                                | required | Content type uid, e.g. `api::article.article`.                                                                                                                                  |
| `actions`  | `Array` | all six  | Actions that send an event.                                                                                                                                                     |
| `populate` | `'*' \| true \| string[] \| object`                                                     | none     | Relations to load before `create`, `update`, `publish` and `discardDraft` are sent. `'*'` and `true` load one level of every relation. An object uses Strapi's populate syntax. |

Events are named `:`, for example `article:publish`.
Content types set here appear as read-only rows in the admin settings.

### Payloads

| Action                                        | Payload                                  |
| --------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------- |
| `create`, `update`, `publish`, `discardDraft` | `{ data: { id, attributes }, meta: {} }` |
| `unpublish`, `delete`                         | `{ data: { documentId, locale? } }`      |

Each role and API token receives the entry sanitized with its own Content API
permissions. Populated relations it cannot read are removed. Keep `populate`
small: every relation is loaded once per event and sanitized once per
listening role or token.

## `sensitiveFields`

Field names removed from every content event and from `strapi.$io.raw()`
payloads, at any depth. The built-in list already covers `password`,
`resetPasswordToken`, `confirmationToken`, `apiKey`, `secret` and similar keys,
as well as fields marked `private` in the schema.

```js
sensitiveFields: ['internalNotes', 'costPrice'],
```

Editors can add more under _Settings > Socket.IO > Content events > Excluded fields_.

## `events`

```js
events: [
  { name: 'connection', handler: ({ strapi }, socket) => strapi.log.debug(`[io] ${socket.id} connected`) },
  { name: 'ping', handler: (_ctx, socket, ...args) => args.at(-1)?.('pong') },
],
```

| Key       | Type                                           | Description                                               |
| --------- | ---------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------- |
| `name`    | `string`                                       | Client event name. `connection` runs once per new socket. |
| `handler` | `({ strapi, io }, socket, ...args) => unknown` | `io` is `strapi.$io`. Errors are caught and logged.       |
| `admin`   | `boolean`                                      | Also run on admin presence sockets. Default `false`.      |

Check `socket.data.kind` (`public`, `user`, `token` or `admin`) before you use
an id. Full guide: [Custom events](/examples/events).

## `hooks.init`

```js
hooks: {
  async init({ strapi, $io }) {
    $io.server.use((socket, next) => next());
  },
},
```

- Awaited during bootstrap. The HTTP server is not listening yet.
- Middleware added with `$io.server.use()` runs before the plugin handshake.
- `$io` and `io` are the same object (`io` is kept for configs written for older versions).
- An error is logged as `[io] hooks.init failed` and Strapi keeps starting.

Full guide with the Redis adapter: [Hooks](/examples/hooks).

## `socket.serverOptions`

Passed to Socket.IO's [`new Server(httpServer, options)`](https://socket.io/docs/v4/server-options/).
The plugin sets these defaults; anything you set wins.

| Option                                          | Plugin default          | Why                                                                                                     |
| ----------------------------------------------- | ----------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `destroyUpgrade`                                | `false`                 | Other WebSocket upgrades on Strapi's server (Data Transfer) are left to Strapi instead of being closed. |
| `maxHttpBufferSize`                             | `1e5` (100 KB)          | Caps the size of a client message. Socket.IO's own default is 1 MB.                                     |
| `cors`                                          | from _Allowed origins_  | CORS headers for listed origins only.                                                                   |
| `allowRequest`                                  | from _Allowed origins_  | Refuses polling and WebSocket requests from browser origins that are not allowed.                       |
| `pingInterval`, `pingTimeout`, `connectTimeout` | from the admin settings | Applied to new connections without a restart.                                                           |

Setting `cors` or `allowRequest` yourself turns off the admin setting
_Allowed origins_ for that option.

```js
socket: {
  serverOptions: {
    path: '/realtime', // clients then connect with io(url, { path: '/realtime' })
    maxHttpBufferSize: 1e6,
  },
},
```

## Admin settings

_Settings > Socket.IO > Settings_. Changes apply to new connections without a
restart. Stored in Strapi's plugin store and validated with a strict schema.

| Setting                      | Default              | Description                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| ---------------------------- | -------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Allowed origins              | none                 | Browser origins that may connect. With an empty list only the Strapi host itself and the origins of `server.url` / `admin.url` are allowed. Clients without an `Origin` header (servers, mobile apps) are always allowed. |
| Maximum connections          | `0` (no limit)       | Refuses new connections above this number.                                                                                                                                                                                |
| Ping interval / timeout      | `25000` / `20000` ms | Socket.IO heartbeat.                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| Connection timeout           | `45000` ms           | Time a client has to finish the handshake.                                                                                                                                                                                |
| Require authentication       | off                  | Refuse clients without a JWT or API token.                                                                                                                                                                                |
| Limit client events          | off, `10`/s          | Per-client event limit.                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| Allowed / blocked IPs        | none                 | IPv4/IPv6 addresses and CIDR blocks. The client IP follows Strapi's `server.proxy` settings.                                                                                                                              |
| Only published content       | on                   | Do not send draft versions.                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| Excluded fields              | none                 | Field names never sent.                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| Content types and actions    | none                 | Watch more API content types without a deploy.                                                                                                                                                                            |
| Roles: allow connection      | all allowed          | Refuse sockets of a Users & Permissions role. What a role receives follows its permissions.                                                                                                                               |
| Entry subscriptions, limit   | off, `100`           | Let clients follow single entries with `subscribe-entity` (1 to 1,000 per client). Needs read permission of the client's role or token.                                                                                   |
| Show who is editing / typing | on / on              | Live presence in the Content Manager.                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| Log connections              | off                  | Info log line per connect and disconnect (no IPs or tokens).                                                                                                                                                              |
| Event log, size              | off, `100`           | In-memory list of recent events for _Monitoring_.                                                                                                                                                                         |

The section _Export and import_ downloads the saved settings as JSON (no
secrets) and imports such a file: the server checks it with the same schema
(`POST /io/settings/validate`, needs _Update settings_), the changed values
are listed for confirmation and fill the form, and nothing is stored until
_Save_.

## Environment variables

The plugin reads none itself. Use Strapi's `env()` helper in your config:

```js
module.exports = ({ env }) => ({
  io: {
    enabled: env.bool('IO_ENABLED', true),
    config: {
      contentTypes: ['api::article.article'],
      socket: { serverOptions: { path: env('IO_PATH', '/socket.io') } },
    },
  },
});
```

## See also

- [IO class](/api/io-class): `strapi.$io` methods
- [Custom events](/examples/events) and [Hooks](/examples/hooks)
- [Socket.IO server options](https://socket.io/docs/v4/server-options/)


========== https://strapi-community.github.io/plugin-io/examples/ ==========

# Examples

Short, working examples. Each one assumes Strapi 5, the plugin installed and
the role or token used by the client allowed to **find** the content type.

- [Content types](/examples/content-types): which events are sent and how to shape them
- [Custom events](/examples/events): handle events your clients send
- [Hooks](/examples/hooks): Redis adapter, middleware, namespaces

## Live article list

```js
// config/plugins.js
module.exports = {
  io: { enabled: true, config: { contentTypes: ['api::article.article'] } },
};
```

```js
// browser
import { io } from 'socket.io-client';

const socket = io('https://cms.example.com');

socket.on('article:publish', ({ data }) => upsert(data.id, data.attributes));
socket.on('article:update', ({ data }) => upsert(data.id, data.attributes));
socket.on('article:unpublish', ({ data }) => remove(data.documentId));
socket.on('article:delete', ({ data }) => remove(data.documentId));
```

`publish`, `update`, `create` and `discardDraft` carry the sanitized entry as
`{ data: { id, attributes }, meta }`. `unpublish` and `delete` carry
`{ data: { documentId, locale? } }`.

## Signed-in users only

Users & Permissions JWTs put the client in the room of its role, so it
receives what that role may read.

```js
const socket = io('https://cms.example.com', {
  // a function runs on every (re)connect, so a refreshed token is used
  auth: (cb) => cb({ strategy: 'jwt', token: getJwt() }),
});

socket.on('connect_error', (error) => console.warn(error.message)); // "Authentication failed"
```

Turn on _Require authentication_ in _Settings > Socket.IO_ to refuse clients
without a token.

## Server-to-server with an API token

```js
const socket = io('https://cms.example.com', {
  auth: { strategy: 'api-token', token: process.env.STRAPI_READ_TOKEN },
});
socket.on('order:create', ({ data }) => fulfil(data));
```

Read-only and full-access content API tokens receive every watched content
type; custom tokens receive the types they may `find` or `findOne`.

## Notify one user

```js
// config/plugins.js: put each signed-in user in a personal room
events: [
  {
    name: 'connection',
    handler(_ctx, socket) {
      if (socket.data.kind === 'user') socket.join(`user-${socket.data.user.id}`);
    },
  },
],
```

```js
// anywhere in Strapi, e.g. a service
strapi.$io.server.to(`user-${userId}`).emit('notification', { text: 'Your export is ready' });
```

For a payload that might contain secrets, use `strapi.$io.raw({ event, data, rooms })`,
which removes sensitive keys first.

## Broadcast a maintenance notice

```js
await strapi.$io.raw({ event: 'maintenance', data: { startsAt: '22:00 UTC' } });
```

Without `rooms` the event goes to every connected client.

## Chat, typing and online status

See [Custom events](/examples/events) for a chat with access-checked rooms,
a typing indicator and online status.

## Content Manager presence

Nothing to code: the plugin adds a _Live presence_ panel to the edit view that
shows which other admins have the same entry open. Admins only see entries of
content types they may read. Turn it off in _Settings > Socket.IO > Live presence_.

## React

```tsx
import { useEffect, useState } from 'react';
import { io, type Socket } from 'socket.io-client';

export function useArticles(url: string, getToken?: () => string | undefined) {
  const [articles, setArticles] = useState>({});

  useEffect(() => {
    const socket: Socket = io(url, {
      auth: (cb) => {
        const token = getToken?.();
        cb(token ? { strategy: 'jwt', token } : {});
      },
    });
    const upsert = ({ data }: { data: { id: number; attributes: unknown } }) =>
      setArticles((prev) => ({ ...prev, [data.id]: data.attributes }));
    socket.on('article:publish', upsert);
    socket.on('article:update', upsert);
    return () => {
      socket.disconnect();
    };
  }, [url, getToken]);

  return articles;
}
```

## Vue 3

```ts
import { onBeforeUnmount, ref } from 'vue';
import { io } from 'socket.io-client';

export function useArticles(url: string) {
  const articles = ref>({});
  const socket = io(url);
  const upsert = ({ data }: { data: { id: number; attributes: unknown } }) => {
    articles.value = { ...articles.value, [data.id]: data.attributes };
  };
  socket.on('article:publish', upsert);
  socket.on('article:update', upsert);
  onBeforeUnmount(() => socket.disconnect());
  return { articles };
}
```

## Next.js (App Router)

Socket.IO clients run in the browser, so use them in a client component:

```tsx
'use client';
import { useEffect } from 'react';
import { io } from 'socket.io-client';
import { useRouter } from 'next/navigation';

export function LiveRefresh() {
  const router = useRouter();
  useEffect(() => {
    const socket = io(process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_STRAPI_URL!);
    socket.on('article:publish', () => router.refresh());
    return () => {
      socket.disconnect();
    };
  }, [router]);
  return null;
}
```

If the site and Strapi run on different origins, add the site's origin under
_Settings > Socket.IO > Allowed origins_.

## Test an integration

```js
const assert = require('node:assert/strict');
const test = require('node:test');
const { io } = require('socket.io-client');

test('a published article reaches the public role', async () => {
  const socket = io(process.env.STRAPI_URL, { transports: ['websocket'] });
  const event = new Promise((resolve) => socket.once('article:publish', resolve));
  await publishTestArticle(); // your helper, e.g. a REST call with an API token
  const { data } = await event;
  assert.equal(data.attributes.title, 'Test article');
  socket.close();
});
```

## Need help?

Open an issue on [GitHub](https://github.com/strapi-community/plugin-io/issues)
with your Strapi version, plugin version and the smallest config that shows the
problem.


========== https://strapi-community.github.io/plugin-io/examples/content-types ==========

# Content types

A watched content type sends an event after every matching Document Service
action. The event goes to each Users & Permissions role and content API token
that may read the type, sanitized with that audience's permissions.

## Watch everything

```js
// config/plugins.js
module.exports = {
  io: {
    enabled: true,
    config: {
      contentTypes: ['api::article.article', 'api::category.category'],
    },
  },
};
```

A string watches all six actions.

| Action         | Event                  | When                                          | Payload                                  |
| -------------- | ---------------------- | --------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------- |
| `create`       | `article:create`       | A document is created                         | `{ data: { id, attributes }, meta: {} }` |
| `update`       | `article:update`       | A document is updated                         | `{ data: { id, attributes }, meta: {} }` |
| `publish`      | `article:publish`      | A draft is published                          | `{ data: { id, attributes }, meta: {} }` |
| `discardDraft` | `article:discardDraft` | A draft is reset to the published version     | `{ data: { id, attributes }, meta: {} }` |
| `unpublish`    | `article:unpublish`    | A document is unpublished                     | `{ data: { documentId, locale? } }`      |
| `delete`       | `article:delete`       | A document, or one of its locales, is deleted | `{ data: { documentId, locale? } }`      |

The event name uses the content type's `singularName`.

## Pick actions

```js
contentTypes: [
  { uid: 'api::article.article', actions: ['publish', 'unpublish', 'delete'] },
  { uid: 'api::order.order', actions: ['create'] },
],
```

Editors can also watch API content types and toggle actions in
_Settings > Socket.IO > Settings > Content events_. Types set in the config
show there as read-only rows.

## Populate relations

```js
contentTypes: [
  { uid: 'api::article.article', populate: ['author', 'cover'] },
  { uid: 'api::page.page', populate: { seo: { fields: ['metaTitle'] } } },
  { uid: 'api::product.product', populate: '*' },
],
```

Before the event is sent, the entry is fetched again with the same locale and
status and the given `populate`. Relations arrive in the v4-style shape
`{ data: { id, attributes } }`:

```js
socket.on('article:publish', ({ data }) => {
  const author = data.attributes.author?.data?.attributes;
  console.log(data.attributes.title, 'by', author?.username);
});
```

A role that may not read the related type receives the entry without that
relation. Populate only what clients need: every relation costs a query per
event.

## Drafts

With Draft & Publish, draft versions are not sent while
_Only published content_ is on (the default). Listen to `:publish` for new
content. Turn the setting off to send `create` and `update` for drafts to the
roles that may read them.

## Locales

Each locale is its own event. Delete and unpublish payloads include `locale`
for localized content:

```js
socket.on('article:delete', ({ data }) => removeFromList(data.documentId, data.locale));
```

## Keep a list in sync

```js
const articles = new Map(); // documentId -> attributes

const upsert = ({ data }) => articles.set(data.attributes.documentId, data.attributes);
const remove = ({ data }) => articles.delete(data.documentId);

socket.on('article:publish', upsert);
socket.on('article:update', upsert);
socket.on('article:unpublish', remove);
socket.on('article:delete', remove);
```

Load the initial list through the REST API, then apply events. After a
reconnect, reload the list, since events sent while a client was offline are
not replayed.

## What is never sent

- Fields marked `private` and password fields (Strapi's Content API sanitizer).
- Fields the audience may not read.
- Built-in secret names (`password`, `resetPasswordToken`, `apiKey`, `secret`, ...), `config.sensitiveFields` and the _Excluded fields_ setting.

If sanitizing fails for an audience, that audience gets nothing. The plugin
never falls back to the raw entry.

## Events from your own code

Events come from the Document Service, so `strapi.documents(uid).update(...)`
in your services emits them too. `strapi.db.query()` writes do not. To send
something yourself:

```js
// sanitized per audience, like the automatic events
await strapi.$io.emit({ event: 'update', schema: 'api::article.article', data: entry });

// a custom event, sensitive keys removed
await strapi.$io.raw({ event: 'stock:low', data: { sku: 'A-1', left: 3 }, rooms: ['io-role-authenticated'] });
```

## Troubleshooting

| Symptom                           | Check                                                                       |
| --------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| No events at all                  | The role or token has `find` or `findOne` on the type. The type is watched. |
| `create` arrives but not drafts   | _Only published content_ is on (default). Listen to `:publish`.             |
| Relation missing                  | It is not in `populate`, or the audience may not read the related type.     |
| Writes from a script send nothing | The script uses `strapi.db.query()`. Use `strapi.documents()`.              |

## See also

- [Plugin configuration](/api/plugin-config)
- [IO class](/api/io-class)
- [Strapi Document Service](https://docs.strapi.io/cms/api/document-service)


========== https://strapi-community.github.io/plugin-io/examples/events ==========

# Custom events

`config.events` registers handlers for events your clients send. The plugin
authenticates the socket first, so every handler can check who is talking.

```js
// config/plugins.js
module.exports = {
  io: {
    enabled: true,
    config: {
      contentTypes: ['api::article.article'],
      events: [
        { name: 'connection', handler: ({ strapi }, socket) => strapi.log.debug(`[io] ${socket.id} connected`) },
        { name: 'ping', handler: (_ctx, socket) => socket.emit('pong', { at: Date.now() }) },
      ],
    },
  },
};
```

## Handler signature

```ts
handler(context: { strapi; io }, socket, ...args): void | Promise
```

| Argument  | What it is                                                                                         |
| --------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `strapi`  | The Strapi instance.                                                                               |
| `io`      | The plugin wrapper (`strapi.$io`). `io.server` is the Socket.IO `Server`.                          |
| `socket`  | The client's Socket.IO socket.                                                                     |
| `...args` | What the client sent. When the client passes an acknowledgement callback, it is the last argument. |

- The name `connection` runs once for every new socket, with no extra arguments.
- Any other name, including `disconnect`, is registered with `socket.on(name)`.
- Errors thrown in a handler are caught and logged as `[io] Handler for "" failed`. The socket stays connected.
- When _Limit client events_ is on (Settings > Socket.IO), each client may send at most the configured number of events per second.

## Who is the client? (`socket.data`)

Always check `socket.data.kind` before you use an id. A Users & Permissions
user and an admin can have the same numeric id.

| `kind`   | Set by                                      | Keys you can use                                                        |
| -------- | ------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `public` | No token (while authentication is optional) | `socket.data.role` (the Public role)                                    |
| `user`   | Users & Permissions JWT                     | `socket.data.user.id`, `socket.data.user.role`, `socket.data.expiresAt` |
| `token`  | Content API token                           | `socket.data.token.id`, `socket.data.token.type`                        |
| `admin`  | The Content Manager presence panel          | `socket.data.admin.id`, `.firstname`, `.lastname`                       |

Admin presence sockets do **not** run your handlers unless the event sets
`admin: true`:

```js
{ name: 'admin-note', admin: true, handler: ({ strapi }, socket) => strapi.log.info(`Admin ${socket.data.admin.id}`) }
```

The plugin's own rooms are `io-role-`, `io-token-`,
`io-admin-` and `presence::`.
`strapi.$io.joinRoom()` refuses them, so a client never ends up in a room it is
not entitled to.

## Update the signed-in user

Accept the event from Users & Permissions users only, validate the payload,
and update the row by id.

```js
{
  name: 'profile:rename',
  async handler({ strapi }, socket, payload, ack) {
    const reply = typeof ack === 'function' ? ack : () => {};
    if (socket.data.kind !== 'user') return reply({ ok: false, error: 'Sign in first' });

    const username = typeof payload?.username === 'string' ? payload.username.trim() : '';
    if (username.length  30) {
      return reply({ ok: false, error: 'Use 3 to 30 characters' });
    }

    await strapi.db
      .query('plugin::users-permissions.user')
      .update({ where: { id: socket.data.user.id }, data: { username } });
    reply({ ok: true });
  },
}
```

Client:

```js
socket.emit('profile:rename', { username: 'ada' }, (result) => console.log(result));
```

`strapi.db.query()` skips Document Service middlewares, so this write does not
emit a content event. Use `strapi.documents()` when you want the plugin to
send one.

## Chat with rooms

Clients join a chat room only after the server checked access. Messages are
saved with the Document Service and sent to the room.

```js
const ROOM_ID = /^[a-z0-9-]{1,40}$/;

module.exports = {
  io: {
    enabled: true,
    config: {
      contentTypes: [],
      events: [
        {
          name: 'chat:join',
          async handler({ strapi }, socket, roomId, ack) {
            const reply = typeof ack === 'function' ? ack : () => {};
            if (socket.data.kind !== 'user' || typeof roomId !== 'string' || !ROOM_ID.test(roomId)) {
              return reply({ ok: false });
            }
            const member = await strapi.documents('api::chat-member.chat-member').findFirst({
              filters: { room: { slug: roomId }, user: { id: socket.data.user.id } },
              fields: ['documentId'],
            });
            if (!member) return reply({ ok: false });
            socket.join(`chat:${roomId}`);
            reply({ ok: true });
          },
        },
        {
          name: 'chat:message',
          async handler({ strapi }, socket, input) {
            const roomId = input?.roomId;
            const text = typeof input?.text === 'string' ? input.text.trim().slice(0, 2000) : '';
            if (socket.data.kind !== 'user' || !text || !socket.rooms.has(`chat:${roomId}`)) return;

            const message = await strapi.documents('api::message.message').create({
              data: { text, roomSlug: roomId, author: socket.data.user.id },
              fields: ['documentId', 'text', 'createdAt'],
            });
            socket.to(`chat:${roomId}`).emit('chat:message', { ...message, authorId: socket.data.user.id });
          },
        },
      ],
    },
  },
};
```

`socket.rooms.has()` makes sure a client only posts to a room it joined through
`chat:join`.

## Typing indicator

Typing events are short-lived, so they are not stored. Throttle them on the
client, for example to one event every two seconds.

```js
{
  name: 'chat:typing',
  handler(_ctx, socket, input) {
    const room = `chat:${input?.roomId}`;
    if (socket.data.kind !== 'user' || !socket.rooms.has(room)) return;
    socket.to(room).emit('chat:typing', { roomId: input.roomId, userId: socket.data.user.id });
  },
}
```

## Online status

Keep online state in memory (or in Redis when you run several instances)
instead of writing to the database on every connect and disconnect.

```js
const online = new Map(); // user id -> number of open sockets

module.exports = {
  io: {
    enabled: true,
    config: {
      contentTypes: [],
      events: [
        {
          name: 'connection',
          handler({ io }, socket) {
            if (socket.data.kind !== 'user') return;
            const id = socket.data.user.id;
            online.set(id, (online.get(id) ?? 0) + 1);
            if (online.get(id) === 1) io.server.to('io-role-authenticated').emit('user:online', { id });
          },
        },
        {
          name: 'disconnect',
          handler({ io }, socket) {
            if (socket.data.kind !== 'user') return;
            const id = socket.data.user.id;
            const left = (online.get(id) ?? 1) - 1;
            if (left > 0) return online.set(id, left);
            online.delete(id);
            io.server.to('io-role-authenticated').emit('user:offline', { id });
          },
        },
      ],
    },
  },
};
```

## Validate input

Treat every client payload as untrusted. A schema library keeps handlers short;
the plugin itself uses [zod 4](https://zod.dev/):

```js
const { z } = require('zod');

const Vote = z.object({ pollId: z.string().regex(/^[a-z0-9]{24}$/), option: z.number().int().min(0).max(9) });

const vote = {
  name: 'poll:vote',
  async handler(_ctx, socket, input, ack) {
    const reply = typeof ack === 'function' ? ack : () => {};
    const parsed = Vote.safeParse(input);
    if (socket.data.kind !== 'user' || !parsed.success) return reply({ ok: false });
    // ...save parsed.data
    reply({ ok: true });
  },
};
```

Do not send error details or stack traces back to the client.

## Test a handler

Handlers are plain functions, so you can call them with a fake socket:

```js
const assert = require('node:assert/strict');
const test = require('node:test');
const rename = require('../config/plugins.js')().io.config.events.find((e) => e.name === 'profile:rename');

test('profile:rename refuses admin sockets', async () => {
  let result;
  const socket = { data: { kind: 'admin', admin: { id: 1 } } };
  await rename.handler({ strapi: {} }, socket, { username: 'ada' }, (r) => (result = r));
  assert.deepEqual(result, { ok: false, error: 'Sign in first' });
});
```

## Checklist

- Check `socket.data.kind` before you use `socket.data.user`.
- Validate the type and length of every payload field.
- Use `strapi.documents()` (Document Service) for content. `strapi.entityService` is deprecated in Strapi 5.
- Answer through the acknowledgement callback instead of throwing.
- Keep high-frequency events (typing, cursors) out of the database.

========== https://strapi-community.github.io/plugin-io/examples/hooks ==========

# Hooks

`hooks.init` runs once during Strapi's bootstrap, before the server accepts
connections. Use it to attach an adapter, add middleware or create namespaces.

```js
// config/plugins.js
module.exports = ({ env }) => ({
  io: {
    enabled: true,
    config: {
      contentTypes: ['api::article.article'],
      hooks: {
        async init({ strapi, $io }) {
          strapi.log.info(`[io] Socket.IO path: ${$io.server.path()}`);
        },
      },
    },
  },
});
```

## Signature

```ts
init(context: { strapi; $io; io }): void | Promise
```

- `$io` and `io` are the same object: the plugin wrapper (`strapi.$io`). `$io.server` is the Socket.IO `Server`.
- The hook is awaited. If it throws, the error is logged as `[io] hooks.init failed` and Strapi keeps starting without whatever the hook would have set up, so check your logs after a deploy.
- **Order:** middleware you add here with `$io.server.use()` runs **before** the plugin's handshake (authentication, IP rules, origin and connection limits). At that point `socket.data.kind` is not set yet. To act on the authenticated client, use a `connection` handler in [`config.events`](/examples/events) instead.

## Redis adapter (several Strapi instances)

Behind a load balancer, every instance needs the same rooms. Install the
official adapter in your project:

```bash
npm install @socket.io/redis-adapter redis
```

```js
const { createAdapter } = require('@socket.io/redis-adapter');
const { createClient } = require('redis');

module.exports = ({ env }) => ({
  io: {
    enabled: true,
    config: {
      contentTypes: ['api::article.article'],
      hooks: {
        async init({ strapi, $io }) {
          const pubClient = createClient({ url: env('REDIS_URL') });
          const subClient = pubClient.duplicate();
          await Promise.all([pubClient.connect(), subClient.connect()]);
          $io.server.adapter(createAdapter(pubClient, subClient));
          strapi.log.info('[io] Redis adapter ready');
        },
      },
    },
  },
});
```

Keep the URL in an environment variable. The admin settings do not store it.
Your load balancer also needs sticky sessions when clients may use HTTP
long-polling (see the [Socket.IO docs on multiple nodes](https://socket.io/docs/v4/using-multiple-nodes/)).

With a cluster adapter, content events are sanitized for every audience room,
because rooms on other instances are not visible locally. With the default
in-memory adapter, rooms without sockets are skipped.

## Middleware

Middleware added in `init` sees every handshake before the plugin does. Good
uses are request logging and cheap pre-checks. Do not overwrite
`socket.data.user`, `socket.data.admin` or `socket.data.kind`; the plugin's
handshake sets them right after your middleware.

### Log handshakes

```js
hooks: {
  init({ strapi, $io }) {
    $io.server.use((socket, next) => {
      strapi.log.debug(`[io] handshake via ${socket.conn.transport.name}`);
      next();
    });
  },
},
```

### Require a client version

```js
hooks: {
  init({ $io }) {
    $io.server.use((socket, next) => {
      const version = Number(socket.handshake.auth?.clientVersion ?? 0);
      if (version  Socket.IO_ instead of writing middleware for them.

## Namespaces

Namespaces you create with `$io.server.of()` get the plugin handshake
automatically, so `socket.data` is filled in the same way as on the default
namespace.

```js
hooks: {
  init({ $io }) {
    const chat = $io.server.of('/chat');
    chat.on('connection', (socket) => {
      if (socket.data.kind !== 'user') return socket.disconnect(true);
      socket.join(`chat-user-${socket.data.user.id}`);
    });
  },
},
```

Client:

```js
const chat = io('https://cms.example.com/chat', { auth: { strategy: 'jwt', token } });
```

Content events are only sent on the default namespace. Use
`strapi.$io.emitToNamespace('chat', 'event', data)` to send to a namespace.

## Join rooms for your own features

Use a `connection` handler, which runs after the handshake, to put clients in
your own rooms:

```js
events: [
  {
    name: 'connection',
    handler(_ctx, socket) {
      if (socket.data.kind === 'user') socket.join(`user-${socket.data.user.id}`);
    },
  },
],
```

Then notify one user from anywhere in Strapi:

```js
strapi.$io.server.to(`user-${userId}`).emit('notification', { text: 'Your export is ready' });
```

Room names starting with `io-role-`, `io-token-`, `io-admin-` or `presence:`
belong to the plugin. `strapi.$io.joinRoom()` refuses them.

## Clean up on shutdown

The plugin closes its own sockets, timers and adapters when Strapi stops. If
your hook opened connections (for example Redis clients), close them in your
app's `destroy` lifecycle:

```js
// src/index.js
let redisClients = [];

module.exports = {
  register() {},
  bootstrap() {},
  async destroy() {
    await Promise.allSettled(redisClients.map((client) => client.quit()));
  },
};
```

Fill `redisClients` from your hook, for example by exporting a small module
that both files require.

## Test a hook

```js
const assert = require('node:assert/strict');
const test = require('node:test');
const { init } = require('../config/plugins.js')({ env: () => '' }).io.config.hooks;

test('init adds one middleware', async () => {
  const added = [];
  await init({ strapi: { log: { info() {}, debug() {} } }, $io: { server: { use: (fn) => added.push(fn) } } });
  assert.equal(added.length, 1);
});
```
